title: unified-rollouts: enhanced canary+shadow AB auto-rollback with multi-metric guards
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Adds multi-metric auto-rollback and safety guards for canary/AB/shadow rollouts. Backward compatible; defaults off for existing rollouts. Enables observability hooks and e2e tests.
commits: feat(rollouts): add multi-metric matching engine and matcher DSL
feat(rollouts): implement proactive shadow-canary controller with staged weighting
feat(rollouts): introduce auto-rollback policy evaluation loop and cooldowns
chore(observability): add dashboards and metrics for deviation-signal and rollback events
test(e2e): add canary/ab/shadow e2e scenarios and stability guards
fix(tests): flake fixes for rollout timing in CI
description: Context: We need safer, more predictable model rollouts across hosted and dedicated deployments. Previous lightweight canary machinery handled simple success/failure counters but did not support shadow traffic comparisons or multi-metric decisioning required for model quality regressions (latency, ERROR rate, token-level hallucination score). This PR implements a unified rollout controller that supports canary, A/B, and shadow traffic modes with multi-metric auto-rollback and safety guards. Motivation: reduce customer-facing regressions by enabling proactive automated rollbacks when core SLO or quality signals diverge beyond configurable thresholds. Changes: - New matcher DSL (metrics_matching.go) to define transparent comparisons between baseline and candidate slices (e.g. p95_latency, inference_errors, hallucination_rate). - Rollout strategy enhancements (strategy.go): staged weight progression, weighted AB lanes, simultaneous shadow mirroring for offline quality checks, and min-observation windows before promotion. - Auto-rollback engine (rollback_policy.go): evaluates multiple signals, supports AND/OR composition, configurable thresholds, cooldown periods, and prevents thundering re-rollbacks using per-rollout backoff. - Controller integration (controller.go): orchestrates staged traffic shifts, attaches metric collectors, emits rollback events, and records decision reason metadata to events/traces. - Observability (dashboards/metrics): dashboards for deviation-signal, per-rollout decision timeline, and a histogram of rollback reasons. - API surface: rollout_v1.proto updated with RolloutStrategy and RolloutPolicy fields; rolloutctl updated to create test configs. - Tests: unit coverage for the matcher and rollback logic; e2e scenarios that exercise canary->promote and canary->rollback flows, plus shadow comparisons. Migration notes: Default behavior for existing rollouts is unchanged. New policies are opt-in via RolloutPolicy on the CRD/API. For rollout definitions migrated from older configs, we provide a CLI migration helper in rolloutctl. Design notes: - Multi-metric decisioning uses a configurable 'matching' window and aggregation (mean/median/p50/p95) to avoid noisy instant decisions. - We treat shadow-only regressions as advisory until the offline evaluation passes X windows; this prevents false positives from asynchronous offline metrics. - SLO-driven thresholds are first-class and can be set per-rollout or inherit org defaults. Safety guards: - Minimum sample sizes and minimum time window before any auto-rollback triggers. - Cooldown/backoff prevents oscillation on flapping signals. - Manual abort via rolloutctl and immediate human override events surface in traces. Checklist: - [x] Implement matcher DSL and evaluation loop - [x] Implement staged weighting and shadow mirroring - [x] Add auto-rollback policy with cooldowns - [x] Add unit tests for policy evaluation - [x] Add e2e tests exercising rollback and promote paths - [x] Add dashboards and event tracing - [x] Update API proto and rolloutctl helpers - [x] Docs and runbook updates Review summary: Initial implementation posted; CI failed lint and one flaky test. Addressed lint feedback (naming and comment fixes) and stabilized tests by adding deterministic time controls to e2e harness. Reviewers Marcus Li and Sofia Ramirez requested: - Marcus: clarify matching semantics when metrics are missing (resolved by adding fallback evaluation that treats missing metrics as 'unknown' and makes policy opt-in). - Sofia: request to expose a compact decision-reason string in rollout events for downstream automation (added "decision_reason" field and ensured it is indexed by our events pipeline). - Ethan: performance check on control-plane CPU usage when many rollouts are active (added batching of policy evaluations and short-circuiting; tested with perf-canary harness). CI: Initial run: failing (lint + flaky test). After fixes: all checks passed (unit, e2e, lint, build). Merge: Squash-merged after approvals. Rollout plan: feature is gated by policy flag in config; enabling requires feature flag flip and minor migration steps (rolloutctl migrate). Observability: Added dashboards and an alert rule: RolloutAutoRollbackRate > 0.5% in 30m triggers Pager duty. Testing: e2e tests added to nightly canary pipeline. Related: ENG-2341 (rollout reliability), ENG-2398 (auto-rollback design). Impact: Enables customers to run more aggressive canaries with lower human intervention while preserving safety; expected reduction in post-deploy incidents for model regressions.
review_conversation: Marcus Li: Why treat missing metrics as pass/fail? We should surface unknowns. — Aisha: Added explicit 'unknown' state and made policy require opt-in to treat unknowns as failures.
Sofia Ramirez: Can we expose decision_reason compactly for automation? — Aisha: Added decision_reason and index mapping in events pipeline.
